title: Merge k Sorted Lists
keyIdea: The next node of the answer is the smallest front among the k lists. Keep the fronts in a min-heap: pop the smallest, attach it, push its next. O(N log k). Or merge lists in pairs, halving their number each round: also O(N log k).

approaches.name: Collect every node and sort
approaches.idea: Put all N nodes in a vector, sort by value, relink.
approaches.why: Ignores that the lists are already sorted.

approaches.name: Merge in pairs (divide and conquer)
approaches.idea: Each round merges lists 0+1, 2+3, … with mergeTwoLists; k lists become k/2, then k/4 … until one is left.
approaches.why: log k rounds, each touching every node once.

approaches.name: Min-heap of the k fronts
approaches.idea: Push every non-empty head. Pop the smallest, link it after tail, push its next if any.
approaches.why: Each of the N nodes is pushed and popped once in a heap of at most k nodes.

quiz.q: Why does the compare class return a->val > b->val?
options: priority_queue is a max-heap by default; reversing it puts the smallest value on top

quiz.q: Why push only tail->next after popping?
options: Each list is sorted, so only the node right after the one taken can be needed next
All nodes must be pushed at the start

quiz.q: Why is merging one list at a time into a growing result slow?
options: The big result is walked again for every list: O(N·k)

quiz.q: What is the largest the heap ever gets?
